questions.stem: India's first PRIME MINISTER + his tenure was:

options.option_text: JAWAHARLAL NEHRU — 15 Aug 1947 to 27 May 1964 (died in office); 3 consecutive general election wins (1952, 1957, 1962); India's longest-serving PM (16 yrs 286 days)

questions.explanation: JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (14 Nov 1889 – 27 May 1964) — FIRST PRIME MINISTER of INDIA (15 Aug 1947 – 27 May 1964); LONGEST-serving Indian PM (16 years 286 days). Born Allahabad; Harrow + Trinity College Cambridge + Inner Temple London; lawyer; INC leader; 9-year jailed under British. ICONIC speeches: 'TRYST WITH DESTINY' (midnight 14-15 Aug 1947, Parliament address) — 'At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life + freedom...' KEY NEHRU POLICIES: (1) PARLIAMENTARY DEMOCRACY — set strong precedents; SECULAR STATE; (2) PLANNED MIXED ECONOMY — 5-Year Plans; PSUs (IIT, IIM, AIIMS, Bhilai/Rourkela/Durgapur steel plants, dams Bhakra-Nangal 'temples of modern India', Hirakud, HEC, BHEL, ONGC, HAL). (3) NON-ALIGNMENT / NAM — co-founded 1961 Belgrade with Tito (Yugoslavia), Nasser (Egypt), Sukarno (Indonesia), Nkrumah (Ghana). (4) PANCHSHEEL — 5 Principles of Peaceful Coexistence with China (1954, Nehru-Zhou). (5) Promoted Science + Technology — DAE (Homi Bhabha 1954), ISRO predecessor INCOSPAR (Sarabhai 1962), CSIR labs. FAILURES: (1) 1962 SINO-INDIAN WAR — India humiliated militarily (Aksai Chin lost); 'Hindi-Chini Bhai Bhai' betrayed; Nehru's health declined. (2) KASHMIR — took to UN 1948, stalemate. (3) BABU-ism + red tape in PSUs. SUCCESSION: died 27 May 1964 of heart attack; LAL BAHADUR SHASTRI became PM (9 Jun 1964 – 11 Jan 1966). GULZARILAL NANDA — acting PM for 13 days (Nehru's death → Shastri). SHASTRI: 'JAI JAWAN JAI KISAN' slogan; led India through 1965 Indo-Pak War (PAKISTAN's Operation Grand Slam + India's Lahore push); Tashkent Agreement 10 Jan 1966; DIED mysteriously next day (11 Jan 1966, Tashkent) — officially heart attack. Ganda acted again 11-24 Jan 1966. INDIRA GANDHI won Congress Parliamentary Party election + became 3rd PM 24 Jan 1966. FULL LIST of PMs: (1) Nehru; (2) Shastri; (3) Indira Gandhi (1966-77, 1980-84); (4) Morarji Desai (1977-79, Janata — first non-Congress PM); (5) Charan Singh (1979-80, never faced Parliament); (6) Rajiv Gandhi (1984-89, youngest at 40); (7) V.P. Singh (1989-90, Janata Dal); (8) Chandra Shekhar (1990-91); (9) P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991-96, first South Indian PM, first minority-govt 5-year term, LPG reforms); (10) A.B. Vajpayee (3 stints — 1996 13 days, 1998-99, 1999-2004); (11) H.D. Deve Gowda (1996-97); (12) I.K. Gujral (1997-98); (13) Manmohan Singh (2004-14, UPA-I/II, first Sikh PM); (14) Narendra Modi (26 May 2014 onwards, 3rd term from 9 June 2024 — only 2nd PM after Nehru to return for a 3rd full term).

questions.stem: The EMERGENCY (declared 25 June 1975 by PRESIDENT Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on PM INDIRA GANDHI's advice) lasted for:

options.option_text: 21 MONTHS — 25 June 1975 to 21 March 1977; longest in Indian history; elections called + Congress lost; Janata Party won

questions.explanation: EMERGENCY (1975-77) — 21 MONTHS (25 June 1975 – 21 March 1977) — the darkest period of Indian democracy. DECLARED by PRESIDENT FAKHRUDDIN ALI AHMED on advice of PM INDIRA GANDHI on 25 June 1975, night. BACKGROUND: (1) 12 JUNE 1975 — ALLAHABAD HC (Justice Jagmohanlal Sinha) in RAJ NARAIN v INDIRA GANDHI ruled Indira GUILTY of election MALPRACTICES (using state resources for her 1971 Rae Bareli campaign); set aside her election + banned her from office for 6 years. (2) JAYAPRAKASH NARAYAN (JP) had launched 'SAMPURNA KRANTI' / TOTAL REVOLUTION movement 1974 from Bihar — calling for resignation; massive anti-govt rallies; even exhorting police + army to disobey unconstitutional orders. (3) OPPOSITION demanded Indira's resignation. To stay in power, she advised Emergency on grounds of 'INTERNAL DISTURBANCE' — signed by Ahmed that very night; Cabinet informed only next morning (violated conventions). FEATURES OF EMERGENCY: (1) PRESS CENSORSHIP — newspapers pre-censored; electricity cut to Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg press quarter; Kuldip Nayar, Lok Sabha Speaker prohibited; many journalists jailed (Kuldip Nayar, Rajmohan Gandhi). (2) ARRESTS of opposition — JP + Vajpayee + Advani + Morarji Desai + Charan Singh + Chandra Shekhar + Raj Narain + over 100,000 others under MISA (Maintenance of Internal Security Act); detention without trial. (3) FORCED STERILISATION campaigns under Sanjay Gandhi (Indira's younger son, informal power) — 6.2 million sterilisations 1975-77; mostly poor Muslims + Dalits; 2,000+ deaths; massive social resentment. (4) DELHI SLUM DEMOLITIONS — TURKMAN GATE shooting April 1976; ~150 killed; Muslim-majority slums razed (Sanjay Gandhi's '5-point programme' drives). (5) 42nd CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT (1976) — 'MINI CONSTITUTION' — 59 changes; added 'SECULAR SOCIALIST' to Preamble; Fundamental Duties (Part IVA); centralised powers; curtailed judicial review. (6) POSTPONEMENT of 1976 general elections; LS extended. POSITIVES (debated): Some economy / strikes discipline. 21 MARCH 1977 — Emergency LIFTED; elections held. CONGRESS CRUSHINGLY DEFEATED: 154 seats (from 352); JANATA PARTY won 298/542 (merged from Jana Sangh, Congress-O, BLD, SP, Socialist, Scholar Party — heterogeneous). MORARJI DESAI became PM (March 1977 — first non-Congress PM). INDIRA + SANJAY lost their own Rae Bareli + Amethi seats. Charan Singh = Home Minister briefly put Indira in jail (Oct 1977 release). Janata collapsed 1979 over Dual Membership issue (RSS). Indira returned 1980 with Congress(I). 44TH CAA (1978, Janata) — reversed Emergency excesses; 'internal disturbance' replaced with 'armed rebellion' in Art 352; Art 20 + 21 non-suspendable; PM's advice = Cabinet's recommendation binding; restored judicial review. INDIA'S DEMOCRACY emerged STRONGER post-Emergency.

questions.stem: The 1971 INDO-PAKISTAN WAR led to the:

options.option_text: BIRTH OF BANGLADESH — East Pakistan separated after India's 13-day military campaign; Pakistan's General Niazi surrendered 16 Dec 1971 (Dhaka)

questions.explanation: 1971 INDO-PAKISTAN WAR — 'BANGLADESH LIBERATION WAR'. 13-day military campaign (3 DEC – 16 DEC 1971); INDIA's most decisive military victory; led to CREATION of BANGLADESH. BACKGROUND: (1) Pakistan's 1970 general elections — SHEIKH MUJIBUR RAHMAN's AWAMI LEAGUE won 160/162 East Pakistan seats + overall majority (167/300). But WEST Pakistani elite (Zulfikar Bhutto's PPP + Yahya Khan military) REFUSED to transfer power. (2) Mujib launched civil disobedience; YAHYA KHAN launched 'OPERATION SEARCHLIGHT' 25-26 MARCH 1971 — brutal military crackdown on Bengalis; estimated 3 MILLION KILLED, 400,000 women raped (per Bangladeshi accounts); 10 MILLION refugees fled to India (Calcutta + Tripura). GENOCIDE recognised by many historians + some UN bodies. (3) MUKTI BAHINI (Freedom Fighters) — Bengali resistance; trained + armed with covert Indian support (R&AW, BSF) from April 1971. (4) INDIA hosted govt-in-exile + refugees; economy strained. (5) PM INDIRA GANDHI's diplomacy 1971 — Treaty of Friendship with USSR (Aug 1971) for deterrence vs USA/China; went to Washington + European capitals to brief. USA (Nixon-Kissinger) sided with Pakistan; sent USS Enterprise carrier group to Bay of Bengal (signal); USSR sent its fleet in support of India. (6) 3 DEC 1971 — Pakistan LAUNCHED PRE-EMPTIVE air strikes on Indian airfields (Operation Chengiz Khan — mirrored Israel's 1967 strike); India formally entered war. INDIAN FORCES: Army's EASTERN COMMAND under Lt. General JAGJIT SINGH AURORA; Navy's Eastern Fleet; IAF; assisted by MUKTI BAHINI. CAMPAIGN: multi-pronged thrusts from Tripura, Meghalaya, W Bengal, Assam; encircled Dhaka in 2 weeks. WESTERN FRONT: defensive; Chhamb, Longewala (Brigadier KULDIP SINGH CHANDPURI + 120 men held 2,000+ Pak troops + 45 tanks — later film 'Border' 1997 immortalised); PAF attacks on Jaisalmer, Bhuj, Amritsar; counter-attacks at Chhamb, Shakargarh, Sindh captured. NAVAL: INS VIKRANT launched air strikes on Chittagong + Cox's Bazar; INS Nipat + Nirghat missile boats attacked Karachi harbour 4+8 Dec (OPERATION TRIDENT + OPERATION PYTHON) — sank Pakistani destroyers + oil depots — NAVY DAY 4 DEC commemorates. 16 DECEMBER 1971 — PAKISTAN'S LT. GEN. A.A.K. NIAZI SURRENDERED at DHAKA Ramna Race Course to Lt Gen. JAGJIT SINGH AURORA (joint Indian-Mukti Bahini accepting). ~93,000 POW (LARGEST surrender since WWII) — repatriated after SIMLA AGREEMENT (28 Jun-2 Jul 1972, signed by Indira + Bhutto). BANGLADESH formally constituted 16 Dec 1971. 1971 WAR HEROES: Capt M.N. Mulla (INS Khukri, PVC posthumous), Flying Officer N.S. Sekhon (PVC, only IAF), Maj Hoshiar Singh (PVC), 2nd Lt Arun Khetarpal (PVC, age 21 — Battle of Basantar); Sam Manekshaw (Chief of Army Staff — FIRST Field Marshal). FIELD MARSHALS OF India: SAM MANEKSHAW (1973), K.M. CARIAPPA (1986). VIJAY DIWAS / VICTORY DAY = 16 DEC annually.

questions.stem: The ECONOMIC REFORMS of 1991 (LPG — Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) were launched by:

options.option_text: PM Rajiv Gandhi + FM Pranab Mukherjee
PM P.V. NARASIMHA RAO + FM MANMOHAN SINGH — in response to 1991 BoP crisis; dismantled LICENCE RAJ; opened to FDI + trade; liberalised industrial policy

questions.explanation: 1991 ECONOMIC REFORMS / LPG — LIBERALISATION, PRIVATISATION, GLOBALISATION. Most consequential policy shift in Indian economy post-independence. ARCHITECTS: (1) PM P.V. NARASIMHA RAO (9th PM, June 1991 – May 1996, Congress) — political backing. (2) FM Dr. MANMOHAN SINGH (former RBI Governor 1982-85; 'accidental FM' as economist brought in; later PM 2004-14) — technocratic architect. PRECIPITATING CRISIS: (1) 1990s BoP CRISIS — forex reserves collapsed to ~$1.2 BILLION (2 weeks of imports); Chandra Shekhar govt pledged 67 TONNES of GOLD to Bank of England + Union Bank of Switzerland (May-July 1991) to raise ~$400 million. (2) Post-Gulf War oil prices spike; remittances dropped; NRI bank runs. (3) Credit rating downgraded; loans from commercial banks dried up. IMF BAILOUT: India sought ~$2 billion from IMF; conditions = structural reforms. REFORMS: (1) NEW INDUSTRIAL POLICY 1991 (24 JULY, same day as Manmohan's first Budget Speech) — abolished INDUSTRIAL LICENSING for most industries (keep only 18 strategic sectors — reduced later); removed MRTP Act restrictions for large firms; opened more sectors to private capital. (2) DEVALUATION of rupee — 18-19% in two tranches July 1991 (₹21 → ₹26 per USD). (3) Trade liberalisation — customs duties reduced (from avg 85% to ~25% over years); Replenishment License → EXIM Scrip → transferable; PL-480 imports; foreign trade convertibility. (4) FDI policies — allowed up to 51% in many sectors (automatic route); Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) set up; mostly dismantled later (2017) as sectors liberalised via automatic route. (5) RUPEE CONVERTIBILITY — 1992 LERMS (Liberalised Exchange Rate Mgmt System, partial convertibility); 1993-94 FULL convertibility on CURRENT ACCOUNT (not capital; Tarapore 1997 + 2006 roadmaps). (6) Disinvestment of PSUs started 1992 (minority stakes; accelerated under NDA 1998). (7) TAX REFORMS — Chelliah Committee + Raja Chelliah; lower direct tax rates; VAT began (→ GST 2017). (8) Capital markets — SEBI statutory 1992; dematerialisation; FII entry; Bombay Stock Exchange vs NSE competition. (9) BANKING reforms — Narasimham Committee I (1991) II (1998); new private banks (ICICI, HDFC, Axis, IndusInd 1993-94); new foreign banks. (10) TELECOM reforms — NTP 1994 + 1999 (AB Vajpayee); revenue-sharing; enabling Sunil Mittal (Airtel) + others. IMPACT: growth accelerated (4-5% 1980s → 6-7% 1990s → 8-9% 2000s); poverty declined from ~45% in 1993-94 to 22% in 2011-12 (Tendulkar line); IT-BPO boom; middle class doubled. CRITIQUES: inequality rose; jobless growth; agriculture neglected. MANMOHAN's 1991 BUDGET SPEECH famous line — 'No power on earth can stop an idea whose time has come' (Victor Hugo paraphrase; ending line: 'Let this be the beginning'). Rao quoted similarly about India on world stage. LPG = 'MANMOHAN-RAO CONSENSUS'. Later enhanced by VAJPAYEE (NHDP highway network, PMGSY, Golden Quadrilateral, disinvestment, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan).

questions.stem: The integration of HYDERABAD into the INDIAN UNION in 1948 happened via:

options.option_text: OPERATION POLO — 5-day Indian Army 'Police Action' from 13-17 Sep 1948; Nizam Osman Ali Khan accessed + Razakars militia defeated

questions.explanation: OPERATION POLO / 'Hyderabad Police Action' — Indian ARMY operation, 13-17 SEPTEMBER 1948, to annex the princely state of HYDERABAD into the Indian Union. Also called 'OPERATION CATERPILLAR' by PM Nehru. BACKGROUND: at independence (15 Aug 1947), 565 PRINCELY STATES had option to accede to INDIA or PAKISTAN or stay independent. Hyderabad — largest + wealthiest princely state (~215,000 sq km; 16 million population; ruled by NIZAM OSMAN ALI KHAN, 7th Nizam, one of world's richest men in his time). NIZAM DECLARED he would stay INDEPENDENT (neither India nor Pakistan). Problems: (1) Hyderabad was LANDLOCKED inside India. (2) Population was 85% HINDU but rulers + elite were MUSLIM. (3) Communist-led TELANGANA PEASANT ARMED STRUGGLE (1946-51) against Nizam + landlords caused unrest. (4) RAZAKARS — private militia of Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (MIM) led by QASIM RIZVI — terrorised Hindus + pro-integration Muslims; 40-50,000 strong. (5) Nizam tried to approach UN. SARDAR PATEL, as HOME MINISTER + DEPUTY PM, prepared military action. NEGOTIATIONS + 'STANDSTILL AGREEMENT' of 29 Nov 1947 did not hold. OPERATION: (a) Launched 13 SEP 1948, 4 AM, from 5 directions (Sholapur, Vijayawada, Bidar, Adilabad); commanded by Major General J.N. CHAUDHURI. (b) Indian Army's 1 ARMOURED DIV + 17 DIV + air + artillery. (c) Nizam's army ~22,000 regulars + 200,000+ Razakar militia — no match. Key battles: Naldurg Fort, Shivangaon, Rajeshwar. (d) 4 DAYS — Hyderabad FELL on 17 SEP 1948 (evening); Nizam broadcast surrender. CASUALTIES: ~800 Indian Army + ~2,000 Hyderabadi forces + 42 Razakars killed. MUCH larger civilian casualties post-annexation: SUNDARLAL COMMITTEE (1949, Pt. Sunderlal) reported 27,000-40,000 civilian deaths (many Muslim) in communal aftermath. 17 SEP celebrated as 'HYDERABAD LIBERATION DAY' (now 'Telangana Liberation Day' since 2023). OTHER tricky ACCESSIONS: (1) JUNAGADH (Gujarat, Muslim ruler over Hindu majority) — Nawab wanted Pakistan; ousted by mass movement; Indian troops entered Nov 1947; plebiscite Feb 1948 confirmed India. (2) JAMMU + KASHMIR — Maharaja HARI SINGH dithered; Pakistani tribal invasion 22 Oct 1947; Maharaja signed INSTRUMENT of ACCESSION 26 Oct 1947; Indian Army airlifted; 1947-48 WAR; UN-mediated CEASEFIRE Jan 1949 along LoC (Line of Control). Kashmir still contested. (3) GOA + DIU + DAMAN (Portuguese colonies since 1510s) — annexed via OPERATION VIJAY 18-19 Dec 1961 by India; Portugal refused to leave peacefully for 14 years post 1947. (4) SIKKIM — protectorate of India from 1950; 1975 referendum → merged as 22nd state. (5) PONDICHERRY + other French enclaves — transferred peacefully 1954 (Treaty of Cession with France 1956, ratified 1962). V.P. MENON (Sardar's Secretary) wrote 'THE STORY OF THE INTEGRATION OF THE INDIAN STATES'.

questions.stem: LINGUISTIC REORGANISATION OF STATES in 1956 (first major redrawing of state boundaries) was based on recommendations of:

options.option_text: FAZL ALI COMMISSION / States Reorganisation Commission (SRC, 1953-55) — reorganised India into 14 states + 6 UTs on linguistic basis

questions.explanation: STATES REORGANISATION COMMISSION (SRC) / FAZL ALI COMMISSION — appointed Dec 1953; submitted report OCT 1955. CHAIRED by: (1) JUSTICE FAZL ALI (former SC judge; chairman). (2) K.M. PANIKKAR (historian + diplomat). (3) H.N. KUNZRU (educator). MAJOR RECOMMENDATION: reorganisation of Indian states on LINGUISTIC basis. BACKGROUND: (1) DHAR COMMISSION (1948) — opposed linguistic states, recommended admin-convenience basis. Nehru, Patel, Sitaramayya also initially opposed. (2) JVP COMMITTEE (Nehru-Patel-Pattabhi Sitaramayya 1949) — concurred, postponement. (3) POTTI SRIRAMULU's FAST-UNTO-DEATH (1952) demanding SEPARATE TELUGU state from Madras State → died after 56 days on 15 Dec 1952 → sparked widespread Telugu agitation → Nehru conceded → ANDHRA STATE created 1 OCT 1953 (first linguistic state); later expanded to Andhra Pradesh after merger with Hyderabad Telugu areas in 1956. Sriramulu = 'Amarajeevi' ('immortal being'). This led to other linguistic demands → SRC appointed. STATES REORGANISATION ACT 1956 (1 Nov 1956) — enacted reorganisation: 14 STATES + 6 UTs. NEW states: Andhra Pradesh (merging Andhra + Telugu Hyderabad), Karnataka (earlier Mysore — Kannada), Kerala (Malayalam), Tamil Nadu (earlier Madras State — Tamil), Gujarat-Bombay (later split 1960), etc. NOT all linguistic (Bombay, Hyderabad retained multiple). SUBSEQUENT STATE FORMATION: (1) 1960 — BOMBAY STATE bifurcated into GUJARAT (Gujarati) + MAHARASHTRA (Marathi) after agitation 'MAHAGUJARAT ANDOLAN' + 'SAMYUKTA MAHARASHTRA MOVEMENT' (ACHARYA ATRE). Mumbai = Maharashtra. (2) 1963 — NAGALAND created from Assam. (3) 1966 — PUNJABI SUBA movement — PUNJAB reorganised into PUNJAB (Punjabi) + HARYANA (Hindi) + HP additions. (4) 1971 — HIMACHAL PRADESH full statehood. (5) 1972 — TRIPURA, MEGHALAYA, MANIPUR full statehood from NE. (6) 1975 — SIKKIM merged as 22nd state. (7) 1987 — MIZORAM + ARUNACHAL PRADESH + GOA full statehood. (8) 2000 (1 Nov) — CHHATTISGARH (from MP), UTTARAKHAND (from UP), JHARKHAND (from Bihar) — 3 new states created by Vajpayee NDA. (9) 2014 (2 June) — TELANGANA (29th state, from AP) — long movement by KCR (K. Chandrashekar Rao) + TRS. AP bifurcation: Andhra Pradesh + Telangana. (10) 2019 (31 October) — J&K reorganised — JAMMU + KASHMIR (UT with legislature) + LADAKH (UT without legislature); Art 370 abrogated 5 Aug 2019. So total now: 28 STATES + 8 UTs. UTs: Delhi, Puducherry, J&K (with legislature); Chandigarh, Andaman + Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra + Nagar Haveli + Daman + Diu (merged 2020), Ladakh (without legislature). ART 3 empowers Parliament to reorganise states. NEW state demands pending: Gorkhaland (WB Darjeeling), Vidarbha, Bundelkhand, Bodoland, Kodagu, Kongu, Greater Tipraland, Saurashtra.

questions.stem: OPERATION BLUE STAR (June 1984) at the Golden Temple, Amritsar, aimed at:

options.option_text: Flushing out Sikh militants led by JARNAIL SINGH BHINDRANWALE from AKAL TAKHT; military action 3-8 Jun 1984; 500+ killed; led to Indira's assassination 31 Oct

questions.explanation: OPERATION BLUE STAR — Indian Army military operation at HARMANDIR SAHIB (GOLDEN TEMPLE), Amritsar, 1-10 JUNE 1984 (main action 3-8 June). Most controversial internal security operation in Indian history. BACKGROUND: (1) Since 1970s, SIKH SEPARATISM grew — demands for KHALISTAN (independent Sikh state); Anandpur Sahib Resolution 1973. (2) JARNAIL SINGH BHINDRANWALE — charismatic Sikh leader + head of Damdami Taksal; initially used by Congress against Akalis, later uncontrollable. (3) Bhindranwale entrenched in AKAL TAKHT (highest temporal seat of Sikh religion, opposite sanctum sanctorum) by 1983 with armed followers (~150-300); massive fortifications, weapons, GEN. SHABEG SINGH (ex-Indian Army Major General, dismissed; trained militants). (4) Bhindranwale's supporters carried out targeted killings (Lala Jagat Narain, DIG A.S. Atwal — shot inside temple complex April 1983). (5) PM INDIRA GANDHI's Punjab governance reached a breaking point. OPERATION: (a) June 1-2 — Punjab sealed; curfew; media + foreigners barred. (b) 3-4 June — army moved in, INDIAN ARMY's WESTERN COMMAND, Lt Gen KULDIP SINGH BRAR commanded ground op; Army built up Operation Blue Star command at Amritsar + Chakrata. (c) 5 June — attack started after speakers + negotiations failed; initial plan 'surgical' (only Akal Takht); TANKS + ARTILLERY deployed when infantry assault failed (Vijayanta tanks + 105 mm artillery). (d) 6 June — AKAL TAKHT BADLY DAMAGED (holiest of holy spaces for Sikhs); BHINDRANWALE KILLED (body recovered 7 June); SHABEG SINGH KILLED. (e) 8 June — operation concluded. CASUALTIES: Official — 83 army personnel + 492 terrorists/civilians dead; unofficial higher (1,000+ civilians trapped in temple complex; many pilgrims there for Martyrdom Day of Guru Arjan Dev). 35 tanks + APCs used. Also simultaneous 'OPERATION METAL' at 40 other gurudwaras ('Sub-Op Woodrose'). OUTRAGE: SIKH community worldwide outraged; Army's Sikh battalions mutinied at some places (Bihar 9th Sikh Regiment, Ramgarh). PAYBACK: (a) 31 OCTOBER 1984 — PM INDIRA GANDHI ASSASSINATED by her Sikh bodyguards BEANT SINGH + SATWANT SINGH at 1 Safdarjung Road, Delhi (her residence). Beant shot dead on spot; Satwant arrested + hanged 1989 along with Kehar Singh (conspiracy). (b) 1984 ANTI-SIKH POGROM — 31 Oct-3 Nov 1984, Delhi + other cities; ~3,000-10,000 Sikhs killed; organised mobs allegedly led/coordinated by Congress figures; Nanavati Commission 2005, + other probes. Delhi Cantonment Block 32 Trilokpuri mass graves. 2018-2023 convictions of Sajjan Kumar, Kamal Nath named, others. (c) OPERATION BLACK THUNDER-I (1986) + BLACK THUNDER-II (1988) — subsequent police+NSG operations to flush out militants who re-occupied. (d) KANISHKA BOMBING — 23 June 1985, Air India Flight 182 (Kanishka) bombed over Atlantic; 329 killed (worst aviation terrorism till 9/11); Babbar Khalsa Sikhs. (e) PUNJAB CRISIS lasted till mid-1990s; over 25,000 deaths. KPS GILL (Punjab DGP) defeated insurgency by 1993-95; BEANT SINGH (Punjab CM) assassinated 1995. INDIA's WORST internal security crisis.

questions.stem: The KARGIL WAR of 1999 was fought between India + Pakistan in:

options.option_text: KARGIL SECTOR of Jammu + Kashmir (LoC); May-July 1999; Operation Vijay; India recaptured Tiger Hill, Tololing, Drass after fierce mountain warfare

questions.explanation: KARGIL WAR (OPERATION VIJAY) — May-July 1999 — fought in KARGIL district of Jammu + Kashmir along the LINE OF CONTROL (LoC). 74-day war; 4th major India-Pakistan conflict (after 1947-48, 1965, 1971). BACKGROUND: PAKISTAN ARMY + 'MUJAHIDEEN' troops (later revealed to be Pakistani regular army of NORTHERN LIGHT INFANTRY disguised) secretly INFILTRATED across the LoC during winter 1998-99 when Indian posts were evacuated (normal winter practice); occupied strategic heights in KARGIL-BATALIK-DRASS sector (5,000m+ altitude), overlooking NH-1 Srinagar-Leh highway — India's vital supply line to Siachen + Ladakh. MAY 1999 — Indian shepherds spotted infiltrators; Army patrol investigated, came under fire; Capt SAURABH KALIA's patrol captured + brutally tortured + killed (bodies returned weeks later with signs of extreme torture; inspired 'LoC Kargil' film). INDIAN RESPONSE: 'OPERATION VIJAY'. (1) ARMY launched frontal assaults in treacherous terrain (vertical rock climbing under enemy fire); 'heaviest artillery barrage since WWII' (Bofors guns critical). (2) AIR FORCE: OPERATION SAFED SAGAR — MiG-27, Mirage-2000, Jaguar precision strikes on Tiger Hill, Point 4875, Tololing; Mirage laser-guided bombs (LGBs) were decisive. Squadron Leader AJAY AHUJA shot down; Flt Lt K. NACHIKETA's MiG-27 engine failed, bailed out, captured by Pakistan (returned week later via Wagah). (3) PM ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE's diplomacy — pressure on Pakistan; shouldn't cross LoC (self-imposed restriction to avoid escalation). KEY BATTLES: (1) TOLOLING — first major recapture, 13 June 1999 (2 Raj Rifles; Major Rajesh Adhikari martyred, MVC). (2) POINT 5140 (Capt Vikram Batra's peak) — 'Yeh Dil Maange More'; PVC posthumous; 'Shershaah' of Palampur HP; movie 'Shershaah' 2021. (3) TIGER HILL — recaptured 4-5 July (18 Grenadiers, 8 Sikh; Grenadier Yogendra Singh Yadav PVC, among 4 PVCs of Kargil — living). (4) DRASS SECTOR (including Tololing). (5) BATALIK + MUSHKOH VALLEY. BY 26 JULY 1999 — all infiltrated heights recaptured. VICTORY declared. 26 JULY = 'KARGIL VIJAY DIWAS' annually. Kargil War Memorial at Drass. CASUALTIES: Indian ~527 killed + 1,363 wounded (mostly officers + JCOs/NCOs in charge; high officer-casualty ratio due to leading from front). Pakistani estimates 400-4,000 (officially 357 per Musharraf's later admission; unofficially much higher — unmarked graves found along LoC). PARAM VIR CHAKRA (4): Capt Vikram Batra (posthumous), Capt Manoj Kumar Pandey (posthumous), Grenadier Yogendra Singh Yadav (LIVING), Rifleman Sanjay Kumar (LIVING). MAHA VIR CHAKRAS: 11. VIR CHAKRAS: 79. AFTERMATH: (1) Nawaz Sharif govt (Pakistan) forced to withdraw after US pressure (Clinton-Sharif 4 July meeting in Washington). (2) Pakistan COUP by Gen. PERVEZ MUSHARRAF (12 Oct 1999) — ousted Nawaz. (3) SUBRAHMANYAM / Kargil Review Committee → led to creation of NTRO, DIA, HUMINT push, Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (CIDS), modernisation; eventually CDS (2019, too late for decades).

questions.stem: The landmark LAW that made ELEMENTARY EDUCATION a FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT for 6-14 year olds was:

options.option_text: RTE ACT 2009 (effective 1 Apr 2010) implementing 86th CAA 2002 → Art 21A; free + compulsory schooling for ages 6-14; 25% seats for weaker sections in private schools

questions.explanation: RIGHT OF CHILDREN TO FREE + COMPULSORY EDUCATION (RTE) ACT, 2009 — landmark legislation giving effect to the FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT TO EDUCATION under Art 21A of the Constitution (inserted by 86TH CAA 2002). RTE Act passed 4 August 2009 by UPA-I (PM Manmohan Singh); came into EFFECT 1 APRIL 2010. KEY PROVISIONS: (1) FREE + COMPULSORY EDUCATION for CHILDREN 6-14 YEARS in a NEIGHBOURHOOD school (1 km for primary, 3 km for upper primary). (2) NO CHILD held back, expelled, or required to pass exams till Class 8 (No-Detention Policy, later modified 2019 amendments allowing detention after remedial). (3) No physical punishment + mental harassment. (4) 25% SEATS RESERVED for EWS + disadvantaged groups in PRIVATE UNAIDED schools — reimbursed per-child-cost by state. Huge social impact. (5) Student-Teacher Ratio norms (30:1 primary, 35:1 upper primary). (6) School infrastructure norms (playground, library, separate toilets for girls, drinking water, kitchen for MDM). (7) Teacher qualifications (TET — Teacher Eligibility Test mandatory since 2012). (8) No screening procedures + capitation fee for admission. (9) RECOGNITION certificate for schools — unrecognised can be shut. (10) NCPCR / SCPCRs monitor implementation. BACKGROUND: RIGHT TO EDUCATION long demanded — (a) Article 45 DPSP originally: 'state shall endeavour to provide free + compulsory education to all children up to 14' within 10 years (unachieved); (b) UNNIKRISHNAN JP v. STATE OF AP (1993) SC judgment — declared education is a fundamental right flowing from Art 21 (right to life). (c) 86th CAA — inserted Art 21A (formal FR), modified Art 45 (for 0-6 pre-primary ECCE), and Art 51A(k) (fundamental duty of parents to educate children 6-14). ISSUES in IMPLEMENTATION: (a) Learning outcomes still poor — ASER reports show Class 5 students often can't read Class 2 text; (b) Teacher vacancies (>1 million across India); (c) private school quality variance; (d) infra gaps in govt schools; (e) funding — Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (2001, merged into Samagra Shiksha 2018) is main vehicle. Education Cess on income tax provides funding. RELATED EDUCATION POLICIES + PROGRAMMES: (1) SARVA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN (2001, Vajpayee) — elementary education programme. (2) RASHTRIYA MADHYAMIK SHIKSHA ABHIYAN (RMSA, 2009) — secondary. (3) SAMAGRA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN (2018) — integrated school education. (4) PM POSHAN (2021, ex-Mid-Day Meal Scheme) — free cooked meals in govt + aided schools; est 1995; Tamil Nadu pioneered 1925. (5) NATIONAL EDUCATION POLICY 2020 (NEP 2020) — third after 1968 + 1986; major overhaul — 5+3+3+4 structure, multilingualism (3 languages incl. mother tongue), vocational training from Class 6, multi-disciplinary HEIs, 4-yr UG with multiple entry-exit, National Research Foundation, multilingual higher education. (6) DIKSHA platform for teachers. (7) PM SHRI (2022) — 14,500 model schools to showcase NEP. GER (Gross Enrolment Ratio): primary >99%, secondary ~70%, higher ed ~28% (2022 AISHE — need to hit 50% per NEP). Literacy: 77.7% (2021 census delayed; est 82%+ now).

questions.stem: The ARTICLE 370 providing SPECIAL STATUS to JAMMU + KASHMIR was ABROGATED on:

options.option_text: 5 AUGUST 2019 — Presidential Orders + Parliament Resolution; J&K bifurcated into 2 UTs (J&K with LA + Ladakh without); status effective 31 Oct 2019

questions.explanation: ABROGATION OF ARTICLE 370 — 5 AUGUST 2019. ACTIONS: (1) PRESIDENT issued 'CONSTITUTION (Application to JAMMU + KASHMIR) ORDER, 2019' (CO 272) under Art 370(1) — extended ALL PROVISIONS of the Constitution to J&K + replaced 'Constituent Assembly' with 'Legislative Assembly' in Art 370(3) procedure. (2) PARLIAMENT passed RESOLUTION recommending to the President to declare Art 370 INOPERATIVE (5-6 Aug 2019, Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha, Home Minister Amit Shah moved). President issued another order under Art 370(3). (3) JAMMU + KASHMIR REORGANISATION ACT 2019 passed by Parliament on 5 + 6 Aug; assented by President 9 Aug 2019. BIFURCATED J&K STATE into TWO UNION TERRITORIES: (a) UT of JAMMU + KASHMIR — with Legislative Assembly (like Delhi, Puducherry). (b) UT of LADAKH — without Legislative Assembly; directly administered. Came into effect 31 OCTOBER 2019 (Sardar Patel Jayanti, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas). BACKGROUND: (1) Article 370 was inserted 1949 as TEMPORARY provision giving J&K SPECIAL STATUS — separate constitution, flag, certain autonomy; Parliament could only make laws on Defence, External Affairs, Communications without state concurrence. J&K state legislature had its own constitution (1956). (2) Article 35A (1954 Presidential Order) — empowered J&K state to define 'PERMANENT RESIDENTS' + restrict property, jobs + rights to them. (3) BJP long sought abrogation (core ideological plank since Jana Sangh era; Syama Prasad Mookerjee's 'Ek Vidhan, Ek Nishan, Ek Pradhan' campaign in 1950s died in Srinagar jail 1953). IMPLEMENTATION: (1) Communications lockdown (mobile + internet) for months. (2) POLITICAL LEADERS DETAINED (Omar Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, Farooq Abdullah, Sajjad Lone, others) — many under PSA; released gradually over 2020-21. (3) 25,000+ Central forces deployed. (4) NO MASS violence but tensions. LEGAL CHALLENGE: (1) MULTIPLE PETITIONS filed in SC challenging constitutional validity. (2) 5-JUDGE BENCH hearing (CJI D.Y. CHANDRACHUD + Justices S.K. Kaul, Sanjiv Khanna, B.R. Gavai, Surya Kant) — hearings ended Sep 2023. (3) 11 DECEMBER 2023 — SC UNANIMOUSLY UPHELD ABROGATION of Art 370 as CONSTITUTIONALLY VALID. Art 370 was TEMPORARY; J&K had no 'sovereignty' post-accession; President could unilaterally abrogate. But directed ELECTION COMMISSION to hold J&K LA elections by 30 SEPTEMBER 2024 + restore full statehood 'at the earliest'. (4) J&K ELECTIONS finally held 2024 (Sep-Oct) — first since 2014; NC-Congress alliance won; OMAR ABDULLAH became first CM of UT of J&K (16 Oct 2024). IMPACT: (a) J&K now fully integrated; Central laws apply (RTE, RTI etc.). (b) Non-residents can buy land (certain restrictions). (c) Delimitation done 2022; 7 new Assembly seats added (Jammu 6, Kashmir 1); POK has 24 reserved seats. (d) Tourism boom; business incentives. (e) Terrorism reduced sharply post-abrogation (1500+ killed 2014-19, ~200 2020-24). (f) Investment push via UT status + new industrial policy. LADAKH demands full statehood + 6th Schedule tribal protection — ongoing.
